component.name: Deck Video Player
component.summary: Controller-friendly HDR video player for Steam Deck and SteamOS

description.p: A lightweight video player built on mpv, designed for the SteamOS game mode: browse your video folders and control playback entirely with the Steam Deck controls.
Beta software: so far it has only been lightly tested on a Steam Deck OLED, a Steam Deck LCD and a PC running SteamOS, and comes without any warranty.

ul.li: Plays virtually every video format, with hardware decoding
Real HDR output under gamescope (Steam Deck OLED, HDR TVs)
Matches the Steam Deck refresh rate to the video frame rate
Audio and subtitle track selection, resume playback
Headphone surround: 5.1/7.1 soundtracks as 3D sound on headphones
Subtitle downloads from OpenSubtitles.com (free personal API key)

screenshot.caption: Library with watched marks and resume progress

description.p: Fixes and a small addition from testing on a Steam Deck.

ul.li: Recently played videos on the start screen
Crop black bars stored in the video (e.g. 4:3 shows saved as 16:9)
B hides the playback controls first, and stops only when nothing is shown
Mark as watched for partly watched videos, including Plex

description.p: Plex streaming, and a security review of the account and network code.

ul.li: Sign in to Plex with a QR code or a link code; servers appear as library sources
Direct play from Plex with HDR, hardware decoding and refresh-rate matching
Progress and watched state synced with the Plex server
Subtitle downloads for Plex videos
Narrower sandbox: Videos, Downloads and removable drives only
R1 +60 s shown in the hint bar

description.p: Better audio and subtitles, and fixes from the first tests on a Steam Deck.

ul.li: Headphone surround for 5.1 and 7.1 audio (audio menu)
Download subtitles from OpenSubtitles.com (subtitle menu)
Refresh-rate matching works on current SteamOS, with an on/off toggle
SD card and USB drives shown by name, with icons
Long names scroll instead of overflowing; About panel
Audio/subtitle choices and delays no longer carry over to the next video
